evaluation_scope.question: How well does the current model separate phishing from legitimate URLs first verified or observed after the cutoff?
evaluation_scope.historical_coverage_rule: Exclude every normalized URL and registrable domain from data that trained, validated, diagnosed, or baseline-tested the current model or its direct raw-pipeline predecessor.

excluded_historical_sources.name: precomputed_feature_dataset
excluded_historical_sources.reason: Feature-only dataset with no URLs. It trained and random-split tested only the earlier 15-feature precomputed model (metrics.json). The current model was trained only on the PhishTank snapshot, the legitimate status archive, and Tranco homepages, as confirmed by exact reproduction of every recorded training count and validation/diagnostic metric (historical_reconstruction_evidence.json). Overlap of the final test with this dataset cannot be checked and remains unknown.

commoncrawl_cc_main_2026_43_official.label: legitimate
commoncrawl_cc_main_2026_43_official.terms: Common Crawl Terms of Use, last updated 2024-03-07 (https://commoncrawl.org/terms-of-use): limited non-exclusive licence; crawled content may carry separate owner terms; no clause specifically covers redistributing URL lists.
commoncrawl_cc_main_2026_43_official.label_definition: Legitimate: capture from CC-MAIN-2026-43 (crawled 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-18) whose host is an allow-listed official registrable domain (official_domains.csv) or its subdomain, HTTP 200, HTML MIME type, no userinfo/IP host/non-default port, and domain absent from the phishing snapshot. The crawl timestamp or a 200 response alone does not establish the label.
commoncrawl_cc_main_2026_43_official.sampling_rule: convert-common-crawl with max_per_domain 50 and seed 42 (headroom for duplicate removal); the evaluator then caps every class at 20 rows per registrable domain and samples at most 1,000 per class.
commoncrawl_cc_main_2026_43_official.coverage_notes: Index records downloaded 2026-11-26T04:02:52Z to 2026-11-26T13:10:10Z from https://index.commoncrawl.org/CC-MAIN-2026-43-index with filters status:200 and =mime-detected:text/html (corrected 2026-11-26; see plan section 7). All 120 domains have a recorded outcome: 76 with captures, 44 with none (the server answered 'No Captures found'), 0 failed; 10301 records in total. Domains with no captures are mostly small US .gov program and utility sites, which likely redirect (redirects are excluded), so government and transport/utilities are under-represented and education, finance, health and non-profit dominate. A seeded re-query of 10 domains returned identical counts for 8; 2 re-queries hit server errors. A response truncated exactly at a line boundary cannot be detected.

phishtank_verified_online.label: phishing
phishtank_verified_online.publisher: PhishTank, operated by Cisco Talos Intelligence Group
phishtank_verified_online.terms: Checked 2026-11-22 (docs/final_model_evaluation_plan.md section 6.2). Stated: free to everyone, website and data via the API (https://phishtank.org/faq.php); commercial and non-commercial API use allowed; open API for researchers (https://phishtank.org/); bulk files offered on https://phishtank.org/developer_info.php. Interpretation: the free-use statement covers the bulk file, but no page says so explicitly. Attribution and redistribution are not stated; cite PhishTank and publish aggregates only.
phishtank_verified_online.label_definition: Phishing: listed in PhishTank's online-valid file (verified as a phish by the PhishTank community and online at snapshot time). observed_at is the per-row verification_time.
phishtank_verified_online.sampling_rule: All rows of one snapshot with verification_time after the cutoff, converted with convert-phishtank; then the protocol's cleaning and balanced sampling.
phishtank_verified_online.coverage_notes: Online-only: phishes taken down before the snapshot are absent, so short-lived campaigns are under-represented. Community-submitted, English-language and brand-concentrated coverage.

cleaning_steps.method: after cleaning, keep at most max_per_registrable_domain rows per class and registrable domain (lowest SHA-256 of 'seed:normalized URL' first); then sort each class by normalized URL and draw min(n_legitimate, n_phishing, maximum_rows_per_class) rows from each class without replacement using random.Random(seed).sample (legitimate first, then phishing)

class_balance.note: Accuracy and PR-AUC depend on the class composition of the test set; PR-AUC for a random ranking equals the phishing share (0.5 here). Precision for each class also depends on prevalence, so results do not transfer directly to a different mix.

metrics.confusion_matrix_order: [[TN, FP], [FN, TP]] with phishing as the positive class
metrics.pr_auc_method: Average precision with phishing as the positive class: sum over descending score thresholds of (R_n - R_{n-1}) * P_n (sklearn.metrics.average_precision_score); step-wise, not trapezoidal.

breakdown.note: For a phishing group accuracy is recall; for a legitimate group it is specificity.

limitations: Lexical-only model: no page content, hosting, or reputation data.
Concept drift: the result applies to the collection window only.
Source coverage: one phishing feed (online, verified entries only) and one benign source built from an official-domain allowlist.
Label noise in external sources is possible.
